title: VM State Timeline
lede: What the page shows once guests and EL2 record the whole IPC notify path planned in the SDK (docs/26-el2-notify-plan.md). Rows by exception level: EL1 (code, ISR, IPC write, IPC read: the receiving ISR) on top, EL2 below (labelled by what it does, coloured by how it was entered). A message's link runs from the carrier tick to the receiver's EL2 entry; a timer's deadline is a ▼ on the EL2 row.

footnote: Synthetic data from timeline.py (seed 20261123), drawn by the same template as the board runs.
boundary: Block edges are where the records were taken, a little inside the real transitions. An EL2 block starts after the exception entry and the entry stub (which saves the guest's registers) and ends before the EL2_EXIT record is written, the exit stub runs and eret returns; those parts are drawn as EL1 and not measured separately. Writing one record in EL2 takes about 0.3–0.4 µs (ETR, 2026-11-23), so this is not negligible. The counter moves in 50 ns steps.
